theyya:
[Thena+ṇya]  CL=7 Theft [theyya] is the act of stealing [corikā]. That which is to be stolen is [theyya]. The action of a thief is [theyya]. Goods that are to be taken by a thief are [theyya]. (Kaṅkhā, Yo, Mahāṭī, 2. 13-5)
[Theyya] is the state or action of a thief. The derivation of [theyya] is by dropping the "na". (Mogg. Pañcikā, 127)
A thief [thena] is one who steals others" goods. [Theyya] is derived from [thena]. (Kaṅkhā, Yo, Mahāṭī, 190. Pāti, Padattha. 265)
[Thena] + [ṇeyya]. A thief is called [cora], and [theyya] is the state of being a thief. Here, the dropping of the "na" should be understood according to linguistic rules. (Vi, Nicchaya, Ṭī, 1. 3)
In [ṇeyya], [theyya] is the state of a thief, with the "na" dropped according to Mahāvutti. (Rū. 387. Kaṅkhā, Yo, Mahāṭī, 2. 1)
[Theyya] (masculine, neuter) means:
1. (Neuter, feminine) Something that can be stolen (such as aromatics, goods, etc.).
2. The act of stealing or thievery (the action or behavior of stealing).
3. The state or condition of being a thief:
a. The mind or mental state inclined to steal.
b. The intention to steal.
4. (Masculine) One who steals secretly or stealthily; a thief.
[Theyyasattha]: [theyya + sattha, with the latter word elided] A training rule (sikkhāpada) established due to monks traveling in agreement with thieves acting as merchants.
Thenanaṃ theyyaṃ, corikā....thenitabbanti theyyaṃ,...thenassa kammaṃ theyyaṃ. Thenena gahetabbabhūtaṃ bhaṇḍaṃtheyyaṃ. Kaṅkhā, yo, mahāṭī, 2. 13-5. Thenassa bhāvo, kammaṃ vā theyyaṃ. Theyyanti nassa yonipātanā. Moga. Pañcikā, ၎. 127. Theneti parabhaṇḍaṃ coretīti theno,...thenoyeva theyyo. Kaṅkhā, yo, mahāṭī, ၎. 19va.(-pāti, padattha. 265).thena+ṇeyya. Theno vuccati coro, tassa bhāvotheyyaṃ. Ettha na-kāralopo niruttinayena daṭṭhabbo. Vi, nicchaya, ṭī, 1. ၎3. Ṇeyye-thenassa bhāvo theyyaṃ, mahāvuttinā na-kārassa lopo. Rū. 387. Kaṅkhā, yo, mahāṭī.
